utterances.text: Which CD?

utterances.text: CD which has on the top this ERN numbers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. So which is going to be the exhibit, the CD or the hard copy?

utterances.text: There is a CD over there. That's one. Look at number 3. It says two CDs. So that's three now.

utterances.text: You should have six CDs as you have.

utterances.text: I joined the French police in April 1988, and I am still a policeman. I am still a member of the French police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when in your transcript it's stated that "In 1999 I became part of the direction in Paris," it's probably also a misspelling; is it right?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's right. I worked in Paris from September 1999. From that date, I worked for the judicial police in Paris. I went to different services. The last one was the homicide detachment in Paris, where I worked from 1995 to 1999, in Paris.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked to slow down when answering your questions. Now I would like to direct your attention straight to your report, and I want to work with the report dated 13th of August and 16th of May, 2003, which is addendum to this report. Mr. Sebire, as part of your responsibility on this case, were you asked to do some work regarding individuals who had been exhumed or declared dead by courts in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. When I joined the Tribunal, in the course of the year 2000, among the tasks that I was given, this was to collect the information in evidence regarding the exhumations and proofs of death for the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct to state that you created two databases?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In order to carry out this task as best I could, it was necessary, yes, to have and create two databases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what these two databases are about?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The first of the databases concerns the exhumations. Inside this database we've entered elements of information that are related to various exhumations conducted in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, also by Bosnian officials, as well as by the OTP. The second database, it had information regarding proofs of death, and this was entered in the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I am not quite sure whether the translation was correct. The second database, it had information regarding proof of deaths, and this was entered in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Is it correct? Is it what you stated?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Not quite, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The second database, the one that is to do with proofs of death, this database was specifically created in order to have the information entered regarding declarations of the death, regarding the people who have died or were missing in the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to briefly talk about the exhumations and then we will move on to proof of deaths. If we take your addendum, your report dated 16th of May, 2003, and start with the page number 5. When working with the database, what kind of information do you receive? What are the sources of information you receive, and what kind of information do you fill in or put in the database?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: All of the information regarding the exhumations was received in the previous years by the Office of the Prosecutor, in documentary form. These were reports of exhumations provided by Bosnian authorities. These were to do mostly issued by investigating judges from cantonal courts. Then these were also forensic and medical documents that were provided. These had been conducted by forensic specialists working for the cantonal court. Then also investigation documents that were done by Bosniak forensic technicians, also sketches that would contain exhumation details, also would contain autopsy reports, exhumation reports. We also received, in certain cases, videotapes, which would include exhumations. These were documents that were used and these -- this was the information entered into the database. We also entered the information that we received -- that we gathered ourselves, that is, the forensic team of the Office of the Prosecutor. We also had a report of the chief anthropologist, of the chief forensic technician, then also autopsy reports of the chief forensic pathologist. Then we've had x-ray reports.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You will have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You finished that you also had x-ray reports. So did you receive some other reports from the forensic of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The reports that we received from the medical forensic team of the Office of the Prosecutor, this was a general report of the chief medical pathologist which was a kind of overview of the -- in all the reports. Also the autopsy reports for each body or part of the body that was examined, dental reports, whenever this was possible. I also mentioned x-ray reports, when it was possible to have x-rays made of bodies. Also by the forensic team, we also had documents, including photographs, and they would include details of the operations that were conducted during the exhumations, as well as the exhumations themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, were you using or have you been using DNA tests?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Not personally. Of course, I forgot to mention that, that among the reports that we received from the medical forensic team of the Prosecutor's office, whenever this was possible, there were also identifications that were carried out by the forensic medical team of the Prosecutor, and this was through -- done through external laboratories, and these were in charge of carrying out DNA testing on bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, can you tell us what information we can -- you told us what -- the sources of the information. What main information we can read from your exhumation database?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Ms. Richterova --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just making a suggestion. We do not have a blackboard or some other kind of large board on which the witness could explain the various templates maybe, but what I suggest is if -- he can direct us himself. If we can identify kind of templates, like, for example, when it comes to the annexes, where you have the reference number, the identification document, and then reference to witnesses, et cetera, that have referred to a particular killing, et cetera. If we could place them as we go along, one after the other, on the ELMO, so he can explain precisely how we can look at the database and understand. Because this is pretty complicated unless it is made very clear to us, and the best thing that we did is that we reserved the cross-examination for some other time, because I wouldn't have expected any Defence counsel to stand up and cross-examine a witness based on these documents without a proper explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible, Mr. Sebire, that we would print -- or you would print from your database the templates so we can see it, what kind of information you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What we can do also, in order not to waste time, we can take -- presumably the witness has a copy of his own addendum right in front of him, and also of the other reports that we have referred him to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, he has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in answering the question that has been put to you, Mr. Sebire, perhaps you could go straight to what you consider to be the page which would help you best and help us best to understand, you to explain to us and we to understand you, the procedure that we should follow in trying to understand the contents of your reports and tables, in particular. This is what is important. And if, for example, it's - I don't know, just to give an example - it's this page from annex 1 which you would like us to see and then explain, you put that, with the help of the usher, on the ELMO and then he can explain to us like that. Because otherwise I think we would find it difficult to follow, the Defence would find it difficult to follow, and anyone in the public that is trying to follow will certainly not be able to follow anything. At least we know the case, but the public doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate it and I intended to go through annexes and do it exactly as you ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: As you are suggesting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect. But also let him choose the pages that he thinks would suit best for the purpose of this exercise, all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure where we finished, but we were talking about the sources of information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now, just generally, briefly and generally, ask you how many grave sites were identified and inputted into the exhumation database?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In all, to date, we have entered information regarding 449 exhumation sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all these exhumation sites relevant to the indictment against the accused?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those exhumations which haven't been relevant, did you exclude them or did you include them?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My question was whether you include them or exclude them.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. The total of exhumations that had nothing to do with the current case were excluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, as stated in your report on the page 8, that after you excluded all irrelevant exhumations, you concluded that 416 grave sites, graves, were found, and 2.019 -- which contains 2.019 bodies?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This is correct. I just want to clarify that these figures are only in relation to exhumations that were carried out by the Bosniak authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to one place on page 8. It's Ribnik. Can you tell us why this place, Ribnik, which is municipality of Ribnik is listed in this chart?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The reason is that among the bodies that were exhumed at the graves that was discovered in Ribnik, these were victims from the municipality of Kljuc, disappeared in the course of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to refer you to your annex 1, and you -- if you have it with you, and if the usher could place it on the ELMO. You already mentioned that exhumations were done either by Bosnian authorities or by the forensic team of the OTP. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This annex 1, you mention that these are just exhumations conducted by Bosnian authorities. Can you just briefly explain what we can see and what kind of information you put in this annex.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This annex we have the totality of the exhumations that were carried out by the Bosnian authorities and we've entered into the database of the exhumations. In the left hand column, entitled municipality, you will see the name of the municipality in which the exhumation was carried out. In the second column you will see the year during which the exhumation was carried out. In the third column you will find the name of the location where the exhumation was carried out. The following column will indicate -- indicates the number of bodies that were found, basing ourselves on the information received in exhumation reports. The following convoy is the -- the following column is the minimum number of individuals that were found in the mass grave. And the final is the -- final column indicates the total number of individuals exhumed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see the column --

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: -- in each municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see the column MNI, which you translated like minimal number of individuals. Can you -- is it your abbreviation which you are using or is it abbreviation used by forensic?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This is an abbreviation which is used by anthropologists and forensic experts. This abbreviation, minimum number of individuals in a particular site we can exhume a number of bodies and parts of bodies, and then, through scientific examination by a pathologist or an anthropologist, we can then deduce a minimum number of bodies that can be found in the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Just to clear this up. I've been trying to follow you, and I think I have succeeded in following you. If you look at the first entry on the first page of annex 1, Banja Luka, year 2000, location of exhumation is Culimi-Kostici and then you have four bodies and then four minimal number of individuals. How do you come to seven, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I put the number 7 there, that corresponds to the total number of bodies exhumed in that municipality. So if you add the three bodies exhumed in Banja Luka, you arrive at this figure, the figure 7. So there are four bodies in Culimi-Kostici, one body found at Culimi-Kostici 1 and two bodies in the Banja Luka cemetery, which amounts to the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I see. Now I understand you. All right. So actually, what you have in the last column on the first line is -- contains the total of the three lines, okay, of the three entries; in other words, the second entry and the third entry, the Banja Luka cemetery and the Culimi-Kostici 1. So you add 4, 1 and 2. That's why they become seven, yes, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. That applies to each municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this page 1, and if we go through the annex 1, we can see some rows which are in grey. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When certain municipalities have been highlighted in grey, or certain sites in municipalities, these sites -- it means that these sites weren't taken into consideration as part of the investigation in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it also mean that that exhumation relates to some other year than the year 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In fact, there are two reasons for excluding certain exhumations, either because the municipality wasn't taken into consideration in the course of the investigation or because an exhumation concerned individuals for whom we have evidence that indicates that they died outside the period of time relevant to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will stay with this annex, but I have to ask you one question. Were you also tasked to find the link between particular exhumation and counts in the indictment, the crimes mentioned in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you prepared annex 9, which is some kind of key to the following annexes which starts on the page 0292792 -- 28. And when I was referring to annex 9, it is ERN number 02927926. Were you using the information which you obtained from these exhumation reports which you included in annex 1 in preparing the exhumations linked to incidents mentioned in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to go through these links later on, and we can deal with them in details, as well with the exhumation reports itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that's necessary, Ms. Richterova. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If we are still in annex 1, I want you -- I want to direct your attention to the page 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the second row, we have exhumation Hrustovo 9, Kasapnica, and we can see bodies, 18, MNI, 0. Can you just briefly explain the discrepancies in these two columns?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I can. At this exhumation site -- in fact, I should say it was a cream sign that was visited by the Bosnian authorities. On the basis of information from the sole survivor of a massacre when the Bosnian authorities carried out the on-site investigation, certain body parts were returned, but not a sufficient number to determine the exact number of individuals present at the scene of crime. Nevertheless, the report listed the totality of the victims, that is to say, the 18 victims that were involved in this particular incident. But the forensic report stated that it was impossible to determine the exact number of individuals present on the basis of the body parts that were discovered. And it is for this reason that one wasn't able to give a minimum number of individuals and an arbitrary choice which we had to make was to say that this MNI number was 0.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you excluded these 18 bodies which were mentioned in the statement of the witness from the numbers -- the overall numbers of the body exhumed; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This figure, the figure of 18 bodies, was in fact excluded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this annex 1, are all the exhumations conducted by Bosnian authorities in the -- within the -- within the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which you were dealing in in your addendum and from which you concluded the numbers of sites is 416 and number of individuals is 2.019, as I already mentioned? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But I ought to add that there were other exhumations conducted in the course of the year 2002 and 2003. Unfortunately, we don't have all the documents that relate to these exhumations. They weren't included in the report that I have presented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there an indication from the Bosnian authorities as to when possibly these updates could be made available to the Tribunal or to your office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To give an exact date, that is to say, when we will receive the documents, well, I wouldn't be able to provide you with such a date now. But we ask for additional documents relating to exhumations on a regular basis. All the documents concerning the exhumations that are directly related to incidents in the indictment -- well, for example, I could mention in the list, in annex 1 that you have before you, if you have a look at the municipality of Kotor Varos, you will see a very small number of exhumations, whereas in the course of 2002, many exhumations were performed in this municipality. We have received certain partial documents which are mentioned in two annexes that have to do with Kotor Varos, and I think that this will be a subject that will be discussed a little later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We know that the exhumations were conducted by the forensic team of the OTP. Can you tell us where these exhumations took place?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The exhumations conducted by the OTP forensic team were performed in the municipality of Prijedor. There were three of them in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your report on page 9, the conclusion is that from these three sites, 193 individuals were exhumed, plus 99 body parts. We will see later under which conditions these exhumations were conducted and why we are mentioning these body parts. Maybe, just to assist the Judges, I would like to show you all the map of exhumation sites so you have idea where these exhumations took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you going to tender it an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So let's give it a number straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And the number of this map will be P2009. Unfortunately, on the ELMO we cannot see properly the colours, but on the hard copies which are in front of the Judges and the Defence we can see different colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist us and explain what we can see on these maps -- on this map?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: You can see the general areas where exhumations were performed in this map. Each colour corresponds to a different body, a different authority. Blue is for the sites exhumed by the BH authorities, by the Bosnian authorities; red indicates the sites where exhumations were performed by OTP forensic teams; green stands for exhumations in which the OTP assisted the Bosnian authorities; and yellow is for exhumations performed by the Croatian branch of -- concerned with missing persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see clearly on this map the locations, and we can conclude that in certain municipalities was great amount of exhumations and in some municipalities there weren't any or just a few. Can you tell us, from your experience, and also based on this map, in which municipalities there were most exhumations?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I would say that there are three key, three principal municipalities: Prijedor, Sanski Most, and Kljuc. These are the municipalities in which the greatest number of exhumations were performed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see also in Bosanska Krupa there is a sign for a site called Jama Lisac. Can you tell us where the bodies came from in Jama Lisac?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Part of the bodies exhumed at the site in Jama Lisac were the bodies of victims from the Omarska camp, the Omarska camp which was between -- which was near the municipality of Prijedor, in the municipality of Prijedor. As far as I remember, two persons were identified on the basis of the DNA analysis performed at the site. The persons concerned were two women who had been detained at the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We need to have a break now. Ms. Richterova, how long do you think your in chief will last, more or less? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think we can finish by 1.45, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. How much time do you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I need probably two more hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need two hours. So we'll only have a 15-minute break, and the next break will also be of 15 minutes, okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Before we adjourned, we were talking about this exhumation site in Jama Lisac, and you mentioned two women who were identified as being in Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember their names?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Edna Dautovic and Sadeta Madunjanin. Those were the two women concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that you testified in details about this exhumation site in Jama Lisac during the Stakic case?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And another location which was conducted together with -- which were conducted by Bosnian authorities together with OTP forensic team was Jakarina Kosa; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness a few photographs from this exhumation to assist the Judges to have some idea how this grave site looked like, and I -- now I am referring to the CD, which Your Honours should have. In your exhibit list, it's under 14 and 15. Do you have your list, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's CD 02129871/0309, for the documentation relating to exhumation in Jakarina Kosa. And the other CD is X009-4467 until 5464. Other is X010-9585 until 9671. And the last part is X011-1196, 1199. And it is also for the documentation relating to the exhumation in Jakarina Kosa. I would like to tender these two CDs into evidence. The first one under number 14 would be P2010, and the other one, because it relates to the same place, it would be P2010.1. The photographs which I want to show you are from these CDs, and it would be easier to go just with the hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So if we could give the witness these photographs, and he can place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Sebire, if you could place it on the ELMO -- no, on the other side. And always briefly tell us what we can see and what you know about this exhumation site. My first question is: Were you present during this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I was present, from the very first day of the exhumation until it was completed. I spent five weeks over there in total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can elaborate, please, on the photographs which are in front of you and assist the Judges with the atmosphere, with the findings during this exhumation in Jakarina Kosa. So on the photograph 0212-9892, what can we see?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This is a photograph that was taken at the very beginning of the exhumation. You can see the area where the exhumation was performed. It starts a little lower down in the photograph and ascends in this manner. To give you an idea of the size of the site, the excavator that you can see, the yellow excavator, is a 20-tonne excavator. You can see its size in the photograph and that can give you an idea of the size of the site that was exhumed. The yellow arrow points to the zone which is on top of the exhumation site, where two craters were observed. In these two craters - in the following photograph you can see one of them. I think that it's visible. You can see its form here - there were rocks in the crater that could be found and there were holes in them. Given the nature of the zone, this might seem to be normal, but when performing the exhumations, we found about two kilogrammes of explosives with the bodies, explosives that hadn't been used, and in addition, information provided to us before the exhumation. According to this information, these craters were the result of explosions used -- the purpose of which was to cover the parts where the bodies had been left. I think that we can have a look at the following photograph, the next photograph. This photograph is quite clear. Unfortunately, I don't think we can see the second crater I had in mind. I'll try to point to it briefly. That's the second crater that was observed above the exhumation site. A photograph taken at the site of one of the rocks where we found holes that had been made. It's a cylindrical form, probably typical of the type of holes that you might find in a mining area. If I may, I'll move on to the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honour, just so that the record --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I thought I had turned it on. Just so that the record would be clear, could the witness be instructed, instead of saying "the next photograph," the number of the photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You're a hundred per cent right. So perhaps, Mr. Sebire, let -- I invite you to go back to the previous four photos and you just go ahead saying the first photo has this reference number, the second photo that I showed and then spoke about has... Okay. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say the ERN numbers, nothing more. Just say these four ERN numbers of the photographs you went through.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Very well. The first photograph that we had a look at, its number is 0212-9892. The number of the second photograph is 0212-9882. The number of the third photograph is 0212-9883. And finally, the fourth photograph bears the number 0212-9889.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can place the fifth photograph. And again, can you please state the ERN number of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The number is 0212-9893 and represents another rock in which we found a cylindrical hole drilled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that these holes were -- most probably from explosions. Did you find any explosions on the site?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: During the exhumations, small quantities of explosives were found. I think one kilogramme, 9050 or something grammes of non-detonated explosives were found there at the same time when we found the bodies. And this explosive was analysed in the Sarajevo laboratory and they confirmed to us the type of the explosive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And all these details are in your report; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Indeed, in the report which was prepared for the Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we please proceed with the photographs. And again, can you start with the ERN number and then indication what we can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Right. So this is photograph 0212-9965, and this is a photograph which shows the state in which we found human remains during our exhumation here. We can also see an anthropologist who is disinterring human remains.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, please. It is photograph 0212-9983?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Oh, 63. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you give us explanation as to this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The chief objective of this photograph is to show different soil layers which we came across during the exhumation. During our work there, we had to establish how deep one could dig into the slope of this mine. And if I can turn to the photograph now, this part of soil here, we have -- in this soil, we, as a rule, have not found any remains or bodies. The area where we found bodies or parts of bodies were here and here. This photograph is purported to show that bodies were found in the same place, that is, in soil of different colours, which could mean that these bodies were brought from a primary grave site to this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mention a primary site, and in your statement you are talking about primary and secondary, can you explain, please, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Very briefly, a primary site is a place where one finds bodies, but no mark, no sign, that any attempt has been made to change the site. For instance, the exhumations which are mentioned in -- for this -- in the report for the Stakic case, for instance, there is a site at Kevljani, and this was an exhumation which was conducted by the OTP forensic team, and I believe that there were 70 or 71 bodies found at that site, and parts of bodies or remains once again about 70, 71, with clear signs that these bodies have been moved after having been buried at a place. So a secondary site is a site with bodies or bodily parts which had been taken over from a primary site, transported to the other side, and then buried once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other indications that this Jakarina Kosa, that it was secondary exhumation site or secondary burial site?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: We collected information from persons who live in that area, and they said that in 1993 - they couldn't give us the exact date - that this whole area was blocked by the army, that numerous vehicles, numerous trucks, were seen moving in that direction; that one could feel that there were activities there in that area; and that explosions could be heard from there, which made us think that Jakarina Kosa was indeed a secondary site. Another element which confirmed to us, perhaps even more convincingly, was when we looked at the names of either persons who were -- either identified there or the names which were found on identity cards found at the site which belonged to individuals who disappeared or were killed in 1992 at different places and other places and at different periods of time in 1992. However, these bodies were all found at Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sebire. Before we proceed with probably two more pictures which you have in front of you, I would like to refer Your Honours to annex 7, which is links between incidents and exhumations for Prijedor. It is 02927917. And you can see that Jakarina Kosa is mentioned for several incidents, or better say the bodies or people who were victims of these crimes in different places were identified in the grave called Jakarina Kosa. Can we please proceed with the photographs. And again, can you please read the ERN number, please.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The number is 0212-9871.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this photograph, we have some idea, but because you were present, can you tell us in which condition were the bodies found in this site?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I think that the photograph is self-explanatory. Unfortunately, we do not -- you cannot see what is written here on this small white squares, but these cards indicate the places where bodies were found, and these parts of the bodies, if you look at this photograph, you can see a spine, some elbows. I'd say that, generally speaking, all these parts were in a very bad, bad state. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I want to ask -- because these bodies were in such a bad condition, how someone would be able to identify these bodies?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As you can see on this photograph, in some cases there was nothing but clothes left. But some identity papers were found inside those clothes, with some of the remains, and we tried to, on the basis of these identity cards, to locate the families, and we also used blood samples and we also requested for DNA analysis. So that -- that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... on your desk. If we can have a look at this.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The number of this photograph is 0213-0067.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what can we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This photograph purports to show the circumstances under which exhumations were conducted here, in this part here. You can see the soil on which we walked, because that is above the slope. And down to about here, at the bottom of the photograph, all this was an area where we found bodies. I do not know whether you can see that this slope is about 40 centimetres long. It is very difficult when you have a -- it is very difficult to conduct exhumations, but you see that the bodies are here almost at these -- that is, covered by 30 or 40 centimetres of soil. But then you can see the remains down the slope. These yellow flags which are seen different places on this photograph indicate that there some of the remains had become to reemerge, to be unearthed. And here to the left, relatively visible, you have these remains and this yellow flag, because there bone had been dug up. So that is all that I can say about this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I said, you were in details talking about this mass grave in your report for Prijedor, dated 28th of August, 2002, and in Stakic testimony. But you mentioned that you managed to recover some identity cards. I would like to show you three more photographs. I'm done with these photographs. Maybe we can -- I'm sorry. No. We can have a look at this last photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we've seen that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No. This is different, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's very similar. It's again just for Your Honours to have idea how the site looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This is 012-9267 -- 2976. It is almost identical with the previous photograph. It is a close-up which allows us to see in detail the human remains that were unearthed. And what one can also see on this photograph and which we couldn't see on the previous one is the fact that here, at this site, are some covers, that is, some witnesses have described the way in which they collected -- they unearthed -- they collected the bodies, especially in Biscani, after some incidents which happened in that area. When they were collecting those bodies, they were asked to put the bodies in blankets, and they also were wearing gas masks to protect themselves against the smell. And as you can see, there are these blankets over some bodies, and also the -- according to the identification that was found on some of these bodies, they indeed came from the area of Biscani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show you this document. It is identification card. And we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's upside down.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. It's upside down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can also find this identification card on the CD already mentioned. Maybe you can -- can you read the ERN number from this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please read for us who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] He doesn't need to. Let's proceed. I mean, it's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. He doesn't need to do that. I mean, we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So this is for Your Honours to see in which conditions these documents were kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just briefly show you another photograph. This is photograph from the morgue.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The number is X009-4862, and this photograph was taken at the morgue in Sanski Most, where forensic examinations took place. And these are the remains of a body marked 209. Alongside this body, the ID was found, I mean the ID which we saw in the previous photograph. And as you can see, this photograph was taken with the head down. This part here is the skull. I do not know if you can see correctly. You can see the skull and various pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, I don't want to go into details in respect to this skeleton, but did you -- I'm sorry, was the body identified based on the DNA?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this body identified as Husein Fijkic, as is the name of this identification card?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to show you the last photograph, and I want to show Your Honours -- this is the person we are dealing with, a human being. So this is the person who was identified as one of the bodies in Jakarina Kosa. From whom did we obtain -- the OTP obtain this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This is the reproduction of a photograph, and it is 0214-4465, and I obtained this photograph after I located the family at the time when we were collecting samples for DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am done with Jakarina Kosa. I have another photographs. I would like to show the witness only two, because I think Your Honours have some idea. But at the same time, I would like to tender into evidence another CDs. We just got them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What about the two that we have already first?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: These are two Redak examination sites. What you have is with respect to Jakarina Kosa; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other two CDs that we have still got --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will go through, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We will go through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If the usher, please, can hand over the registry and the Judges. These are photographs, and they are not listed on your -- in your exhibit list. And it's photo documentation of Redak exhumation site and I would like to hand one over to the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is going to be Exhibit number --?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This will be Exhibit P2011.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, Redak, it's another exhumation conducted by primarily forensic team of the OTP; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Indeed, it is. That exhumation was conducted by the forensic team of the OTP in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to show you this photograph. Did you -- were you present during this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Indeed, I was. I was -- I spent about three weeks there. It happened in June 2000. And there were a number of bodies found at that site. So the photograph that you've just given me has the number 0100-6970-33A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you -- yes, please. Can you describe what we can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This photograph shows the exhumation site at the end of the operation. You see here all the places where -- which were dug up. You see how one went around, the contours of this site. Most of the bodies were found in this part here. So you have it. It's like this, roughly. So we see here the exhumation site 1. So the exhumation was completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Redak is located, in which municipality?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Redak is in the Prijedor municipality and is in the mining area called Ljubija, which is south of the village of Ljubija, along the road which goes from Ljubija to Stari Majdan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Jakarina Kosa, where Jakarina Kosa is located?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In the same area, that is, in the same mining area, about a kilometre and a half or a kilometre from this exhumation site at Redak. So they are two sites which are very near to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you another picture, and because you were present, you can tell us in which state were bodies found in this location.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This number is 0100-6963-03. We see here the work which was done by an anthropologist who was there and whose task was to unearth, to disinter the bodies which were covered here. We see that five bodies were taken out at more or less the same time, more or less at the same time, and each one was assigned a number, as you can see, 70, 74, 75, 77, and 77 [as interpreted]. As you can see on this photograph, the bodies have been reduced to skeletons, although in some places you can see some other parts too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, you described in details the findings from this exhumation site in your report for Prijedor and during the testimony in the Stakic case; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show only one photograph which can clearly demonstrate one kind of injury.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The number on this photograph is 0100-6966-24A. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what can we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: We see the skull of an individual who was exhumed at Redak, and we can see a wound in the skull, on the right-hand side of the skull, made by a firearm. And the forensic -- the post-mortem showed that it was indeed a firearm wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am done with this part of your testimony. We were talking about the exhumations done by Bosnian authorities together with OTP forensic team and exhumation done exclusively by the OTP forensic team. I would like to deal with exhumation done by Bosnian authorities, and I would like you and Your Honours refer to these annexes which relates to links between exhumations and crimes. And if we could go to the page -- or ERN number 02927939. It is -- it relates to the killing of number of men at Vrhpolje bridge and on the way towards the Vrhpolje bridge. We already heard evidence with respect to these killings, and we also exhibited a number of documents. I would only like to present a few more documents. So the Court has the full picture of the exhumations conducted by the Bosnian authorities. I have copies of sketches from the Vrhpolje bridge. I will provide the Judges with the relevant documents, please. And you can see these materials on your exhibit list under number 9 as sketches from the exhumation in Vrhpolje 1, 2, 3, with relevant ERN numbers starting with 00491618 until 1619, et cetera. And also -- and I would like to tender these sketches into evidence. This will be -- because we have four sketches. I would suggest to mark the sketches P2012.1, .2, .3, .4, in the order as it is stated in the exhibit list. You don't need to place it on the ELMO. I just want Mr. Sebire to make a comment on these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just very briefly: Are you aware that we received exhumation documents, or documents with respect to exhumations in Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. These four maps, four sketches, they are part of the documentation filed that we received from the Bosnian authorities, in combination with the exhumations of the sites VM 1, 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were preparing this link between exhumations and this crime, did you review all the documents you identified in your database, or how did you proceed?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In terms of exhibits in this case, basing myself on the exhumation reports that were produced by the Bosnian authorities and testimony of a survivor of the incident that we made a link to, it was easy to compare the names of the victims mentioned by the witness and the number of -- and the individuals that were identified at the exhumation site in Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during the preparation of this annex, of this particular annex or the other annexes, did you work with all the materials which were identified within the OTP?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, as much as we were able to, as well as the specific documentation that was linked to the exhumation documents. I also examined various files of the Office of the Prosecutor in order to find all the documents that would have a direct link either to the exhumations or to any incidents mentioned by the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from your annex, we can see that the exhumation report, an autopsy report were already exhibited, and these exhibits are marked in the annex. I would like to show you a few photographs from this exhumation site.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And Your Honours, these are photographs which you can find on the CD. It's under number 7 of the exhibit list, and it is CD 00437872 until 8218.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this will be Exhibit number --?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this will be Exhibit number P2013. Your Honour, you all have CD, but I have a hard copy, and again, I would like to give this hard copy to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could look up the ERN number 00438102-A -- I'm sorry. 03, 8103. It's page 2. And please place it on the ELMO so we all can see it. And again, my question is: Were you present during the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you visit this place any time later after the exhumation took place?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. I went during the year 2000. At the time I went to the -- when I went to the site, the bridge that we can see here was by then rebuilt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on this picture are the remains of the bridge and the time when you were there the bridge was already rebuilt. And can you show us at this photograph where is the grave site?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The first pit would be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And because you say "first pit," and we also heard Vrhpolje 1 until 3. Were there more graves?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. On the other side of the river, the opposite side of the river, there would be the second pit; and a little bit further away, along the river, there was a third pit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now if I can direct you to the page 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This is 26 of the hard copy. And on the CD, it will be 00438127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] We don't need to go into much detail.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't need to go into much detail. Keep it to the bare minimum. We all know what we are looking at, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour. I just wanted to show the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when this exhumation took place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mean the day, month, and year, or just the year?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I can help you, I am just reading now from your annex, and it says that in 1996 Bosnian authorities exhume 28 bodies from three grave sites. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think he can testify for the Bosnian authorities. You have the documents from the Bosnian --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is from the documents. I'm sorry, Your Honour. It is from the document that the exhumation took place in 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you cannot make any more comments to these pictures, because they are self-explanatory, and I am done with these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: As Your Honour pointed that we don't need to go into other details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think -- you're free to do so if you want to but I don't think we really need to go through the entire --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, I also want to show you one document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And Your Honours should have them in front of you. It is -- it should be under your number 8. It's on-site investigation record by Sanski Most Serb municipality record dated 10th of July, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which document is this?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is document with the number ET 0212-2869. And I will -- I'm sorry. You don't have it. I will provide you with these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, you mentioned this document in your report, or better say in the annex. It is dated 10 of July, 1992. It means only less than two months after the incident itself.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you compare this document with the exhumation reports done by the Bosnian authorities in the year 1996?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the bodies which were identified by this document are the same or are similar which were identified during -- in due course of identification process done by Bosnian authorities; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. For some of the bodies, that's true. There was a report dated 10th of July, 1992, and that was an investigation that was done on site. The authorities discovered it, and this was done on the 2nd of June, 1992, that is, three days after the date or the incident -- when the incident happened on the Vrhpolje bridge. In the report prepared by the municipal commission of Sanski Most, a certain number of individuals were mentioned that were found on location, and these individuals were exhumed in 1996 by Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] What's the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The Exhibit number for this document will be P2014.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to go to Banja Luka, which is the second document in the annex. The ERN number is 02927929. In this document, you refer to deaths of Esad Bender and Omer Filipovic. During your investigation and analysing the documents, what material did you find?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Among the first documents that I had at my disposal at the Office of the Prosecutor, these documents were issued by the municipal court in Kljuc, and then the documents given by Republika Srpska authorities to do with the bodies of Esad Bender, Omer Filipovic. The examination was done by the forensic pathologist of the Bihac cantonal court. And apparently it said that a preliminary autopsy had been carried out on these bodies. Meanwhile, we have managed to obtain autopsy report carried out by the forensic pathologist from Banja Luka on the 30th of July, 1992, and these were the bodies of -- the autopsy was carried out on the bodies of Esad Bender and Omer Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have these autopsy reports here, and I would like to tender them into evidence, and together with death certificate of Omer Filipovic and Esad Bender. The autopsy report is translated, unfortunately [sic]. We have requested translation of these death certificates, but we do not have translation yet. So I believe we will be able to hand over these translations next week. And again to be specific, the reports on the autopsy of the body of Esad Bender and Omer Filipovic, it's document 0229-0926 until 09 -- 8926 to 8931. And I want to tender it into evidence under P2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Wait, wait. Wait a minute. The two certificates which are in Cyrillic script, the one of -- relating to Omer Filipovic and the other one to Esad Bender, what's the exhibit number that you want to give to those two?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Excuse me. Would that be the number for the CD or the number for the autopsy -- the exhumation report?

utterances.text: And when you went through this video, does it contain just the site in Hanifici or just some other sites?

utterances.text: There are several sites that are mentioned on this video also in Kotor Varos and in other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we can play --

utterances.text: How are we going to proceed? Are you going to give instructions, tell us when to stop, and then put questions to the witness? Or are you going to leave it in the hands of the witness to tell the technicians when to stop so that he gives us explanations?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA

utterances.text: And in which condition -- what could you see inside of the mosque and outside of the mosque? In which condition the mosque was?

utterances.text: Yes. Can we pause here.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would object to the condition of the mosque in 1999 unless somebody could associate that condition with the years of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, during the preparation of this report, you stated that you read the statements and the transcripts of the witnesses who have testified or who will be -- who will testify. What did you learn in respect to this incident? And just briefly.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: With respect to this incident?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: A witness who has not yet testified, and pursuant -- a 92 bis statement was received from him, he describes how a group of men was taken to this mosque in mid-August 1992, and they entered the mosque and burned it.
