utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you saw the interior of the mosque in 2000, was it burned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were there traces of burning?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I went into the mosque myself on several occasions. The first time was in the course of the year 2000. And I was able to see that there had been a fire inside. And outside the windows, you can see the traces of soot which are present inside and outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can we play just a short ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you comment? Based on your knowledge from the exhumations, what we can see here.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The board we can see, on which it says "HAN 1/1" indicates that it concerns the exhumation of a body at the Hanifici site. HAN, site 1, body 1. That's what this sign means.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this number will follow the body until the mortuary and during the identification and autopsy of this body; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think if -- we can stop it here. Your Honours has again idea how this went on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, as I said already at the beginning, in annex 9, with the following annexes for each municipality, which is under ERN number 02927928 until 02927990, you tried to establish the link between the exhumations and the crimes. And can you just briefly tell us the method, how you did it?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Very briefly. We, having had the opportunity of reading the transcripts of witnesses who testified before this Tribunal, and identifying the names of the victims described by witnesses as having Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. disappeared, I was able to compare the names with the exhumations sites which had been entered into my database, as well as with the database for proof of death. And on the basis of such a comparison, it was evident that in a number of sites, persons who had been identified by people in this Court corresponded to the names of victims who had been exhumed either by the Bosnian authorities or by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can go page by page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is -- I don't -- unless there is an insistence forthcoming from the Defence. I don't think it is necessary. I mean it's pretty much clear. The method itself I think is pretty much clear, emerges clear from the documents themselves and then it's up to Mr. Ackerman later on to go through this, if it is -- if he feels it is necessary at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: There is another thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think there are very few killings that are contested as such, as killings. The rest -- it's the rest that are being contested more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is another thing which I need to mention, because in these annexes there are documents mentioned which haven't been disclosed, and the only purpose why they haven't been disclosed is that there is a huge amount of these declaration of deaths, huge amount of autopsy reports, huge amount of exhumation reports and other accompanying documents. They are listed in this report. We have written letters to Defence on two occasions, asking them if they wish to inspect these documents. We are more than happy to allow them to inspect these documents or let us know if there is any objection to these documents. In that case, we can of course disclose whatever is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: I'm sure a review will be made, and so long as the underlying documents are made available, if there is any objection, we will make it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And perhaps if they are made available, they could be made available on CD, if possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You say underlying documents. All the documents which are underlying in these annexes, because most of them are underlying. So you want only those which are underlying in this -- in these annexes or which documents you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Just so that I can be clearer to Ms. Richterova: If all of the underlying mentioned but not disclosed documents would be made available upon request, I think that will be quite satisfactory. We have the summary, and if we need to see something we will ask for it. And I'm sure the Prosecutor would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's a very practical approach, and I appreciate that, Ms. Baruch.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I only forgot one thing, and it is the video which we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It hasn't been given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It hasn't been given exhibit number. And it will be P2019. And Your Honours do not have this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we do not have a copy of it, no. That's the video? Yes. I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: That's the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It hasn't been handed to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The video is V0002475.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that it? Yes. We haven't got it, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have it for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: No, you don't have it. We didn't have enough copies of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we don't have it. I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can assure the Judges that they don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I know what I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, before I will move to my last part, talking about proof of deaths, I just want to refer you to the page 9 of your addendum. And if you could just very briefly summarise. This is figures for the indictment against the accused. So for how many bodies you managed to establish the link.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: If we're talking about the connection, I assume one is referring to the period covered by the indictment. 1.872 cases. There's informational evidence indicating that individuals died or went missing in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now I would like to move to another point, another part of your testimony, and it's proof of deaths. Now we covered the exhumations and database with respect to exhumations. And as we know from your previous testimony and from your report, the other database relates to the proof of death. Can you very briefly tell the Judges what is the purpose of this second database?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The second database which was used, called proof of death database, was created after the OTP had received a fairly significant number of rulings by the municipal court in Kljuc, or by Sanski Most, Sanski Most court. These declarations declared that people were -- people who had been declared as missing were in fact dead. The documents about 2.226 deceased persons was received and entered into the database. A small number of the declarations of death, or these rulings, I should say, a small number was translated, and this had to do also with -- as far as the documents concerning exhumations are concerned, the rulings on people who had been declared dead was entered into the database, and this facilitated the processing of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have one example of these proof of deaths, the ruling of the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it necessary? We have seen several of them. Go ahead, but we have seen quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Okay. So I ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- and I also want to mention that in Stakic case, you were asked about the procedure. I just want to point out that one of our witnesses was talking about the procedure and about the law on administrative procedure declaring missing person dead and proof of deaths and it was exhibited under P779, just to complete this. Can you give us the general figures? And I want to refer you to the -- to page 5 of your addendum. And if you could just explain very briefly your findings.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said a minute ago, in total there were 2.026 cases of people who had been declared dead, either by the Sanski Most court or by the Kljuc court. Depending on the information contained in those rulings delivered by these two courts, we were able to determine the period when the person was either killed or went missing. In 1991, there was one case; in 1992, there was 1.174 cases; in 1993, there were 43 cases; in 1994, there were 23 cases; in 1995, 166 cases. In 19 cases, errors were made when entering the information, and these errors have not been rectified to date. We only mentioned 1.774 cases out of these numbers which concerns 1992 because that is the period concerned in the indictment. All these persons died or went missing in the year 1992. However, the information in the rulings indicates that in certain cases the person died either of natural causes or in the course of directly participating in the armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any occasions when the person was later exhumed and identified?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. This happened in 329 cases. A person who had previously been declared dead by a given ruling, when we compared this with the databases concerning the exhumations, we were able to determine that this person had been exhumed. So out of the 1.774 declarations that we received for 1992, we excluded those who had been exhumed, as well as those for whom the ruling indicated that they were -- that they died of natural causes or in the course of an armed conflict. And this left us with a total of 1.277 cases for the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much longer do you think you have, Mrs. Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I really think that I can finish in ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've been sitting for an hour and a half. I don't want to proceed unless I have the okay from everyone. And I can't really see behind the dark glasses. If you let the registrar -- if we only have ten minutes, I suggest we proceed for the next ten minutes and then we bring the sitting to a close. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks a lot. Thank you. So Madam Richterova, you may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, in -- on both these occasions, I mean when you were dealing with exhumation, as well as the proof of death, you were focusing on ethnicity of the bodies, gender, and the time when the person died. How did you analyse the findings, and which conclusion you reached based on the analytical work you did with all the information you received? And let's start with ethnicity of the victims. Based on which is indicated the ethnicity of the victims? And I'm referring you to page number 6 of your addendum, in which you mentioned this. But I want to point out that this was very in detail described in Stakic case. But in reference to Prijedor. So just briefly if you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as the ethnicity of the victims is concerned, the main source of information was obviously the identification of the victim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... what? The analysis points to which direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to all the bodies that were exhumed, for which we tried to determine the ethnicity, 1.300 were Muslims from Bosnia, 10 were Bosnian Croats, 3 were Serbs from Bosnia, and in one case the person was of another nationality, a nationality that differed from the three previous ones mentioned. And in other cases we weren't able to determine the ethnicity. We didn't have enough information that would allow us to determine the ethnicity. In 55 cases we didn't have such information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you proceed with bodies which weren't identified but, let's say, found in one grave with bodies which were identified? Did you exclude them or did you put them into a category unknown ethnicity, or did you draw some conclusion, some other conclusion?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I would say that there are two parts of the answer. In the case of sites for which we had no information, and if the body wasn't identified, in such cases the category would be ethnicity unknown. In the case -- in cases in which an unidentified individual in a grave site was exhumed at a site where other members of that ethnicity were exhumed, in such cases, that individual would be taken to belong to the same ethnic group, naturally. This would have to be verified in the exhumation report in order to see whether there were traces or not of an attempt to change the site of exhumation, to change the grave site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we want to talk about the time of deaths, whether the person was killed or went missing in 1992, what information did you use?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The main source of information to determine the time of death was testimony of witnesses who had survived the incidents in which these people were killed or went missing. This is what we relied on. And as I said earlier on, we received 329 rulings from the Kljuc and Sanski Most courts, declaring people dead. These declarations provided indications on the period of death and also on the circumstances of the death. This information was also useful to determine the time of death. Very often in exhumation reports established by the Bosnian authorities when the exhumations were performed, they would refer to the fact that the site had been indicated by a given witness. Usually this would be a neighbour who was present and then buried the body or the bodies. All of this information was entered into the database. And yet again, this database should be considered to be an aide rather than anything else. And on the basis of all of this information, the time of death was established with a certain degree of precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I will ask you my last question to summarise your findings, I want to ask you something about these proof of death rulings. These rulings, the amount of them, is it the final amount or is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ongoing process?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- ongoing process?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Well, I would say that the figures that I have mentioned are far from being definitive. It's quite possible that in the future, other families might address municipal courts and ask them to make official declarations of death for members of their family. The report that I prepared and the preceding one, from the year 2001, we received 70 additional declarations of death. It's a very small number. It's more than obvious that in the months, in the years to come, the number of cases that will have to be excluded from the 2026 I have mentioned will have to do with the number -- the increasing number of bodies identified in the course of exhumations, the figures that you have been presented with today are not definitive and I couldn't say that these numbers refer to the total number of people who were killed or went missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about if any member of the family survived or is not living within the jurisdiction of these two courts?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Well, obviously, if some members of family have survived, if some members have survived, then applications were made to the courts. But the courts in Sanski Most have established these kind of declarations because the number of persons who lived in Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, Kotor Varos, or other municipality, are refugees, refugees or people who come from these municipalities so who now live in other municipalities at this arrival or other places can go to the local courts. And as far as I'm concerned, I was interested only in those which came out of Kljuc -- of the decisions which came out of Kljuc and Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't know whether again it was correctly translated. The first sentence is: Well, obviously, if some members of family have survived, then no application were made to the courts. But my question was if members of family didn't survive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a little bit -- wait. It's a little bit speculative, because you can't say what happens if there are no surviving members of any particular family.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think we can find the answer in the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Because it can be the member of the family who can request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have my final question, and it's only very briefly, if you could summarise the result of exhumations, proof of deaths, and total number of individuals which we proved to be either killed or went missing in the course of 1992, as stated in your report on page 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Right. With regard to the pronouncements of official death of individuals, in 1992, we have arrived at a figure of 1.872 -- 77 [as interpreted]. As for the exhumations, I indicated the number of sites, then through testimonies, then based on the incidents which are mentioned in the indictment, the number of sites which I have already indicated, so that 58 sites could be linked, associated, with 30 allegations of crimes committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think that we have again a wrong numbers in the transcript, so you stated that with regard to the pronouncement of official deaths of the individuals in 1992, we have arrived at a figure -- and you can see it in the transcript, 1.872 -- 77.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is the correct number, correct figure?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The figure is 1.277, 1.277.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when we add all the numbers, what would be the total number of individuals who were killed or went missing?

utterances.speaker: NICHOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: We arrive at a figure at 2.565. I must add that when we add to the figure declared dead and persons exhumed, there is a slight nuance which has to be borne in mind, that is, that these additions exclude all the of the bodies which were exhumed and not identified. That is, we had from 25 -- from 2565, we have to take out those who were not identified. Which means the number of exhumed bodies which -- for which -- which we used in this addition was 1.088 people who were exhumed from the sites, and we have -- and persons who were -- and those individuals who died elsewhere were excluded from these numbers, and that was 1992. And some other -- that is, we wish to say that there were sometimes duplication between people who were not identified and those people who were found missing and still are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We had a slight problem towards the end of your testimony, but all these figures are clearly stated in the report. So I think I can say that I concluded my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Madam Richterova. Thank you, Mr. Sebire. You will be now escorted by the usher and we will see you again on the 10th of June for cross-examination and perhaps some further questions that might come up as necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Madam Richterova, there is still one CD that has not been tendered into evidence. I'm referring to what is described as the book of missing persons from Prijedor, with ERN number 0212-4008. It seems to be restamped as 0291-3396, 0291- to 3762. 2 of 2. Which is what? You said earlier on, are the two CD's which were then incorporated Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. into one?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you going to tender it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I tendered into evidence just one which should contain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but you haven't tendered as yet. It hasn't got a number as yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So in that case, it will be P2006.2, because it is exhibit to the transcript. And it's /S282.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that we already have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: You have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It can't be S282.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I just realised that there is one more CD, and I would like to tender into evidence this CD at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this was duplicated. This was duplicated. No, it's not. You see what happened? They were two CDs and they remained two CDs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It's only for you, Your Honour, because the registry has only one CD. Because we had -- I apologise that I am making your life so difficult, but unfortunately they at first they did two CDs and later they managed to put these two CDs on one CD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Because what I noticed is that the first one that you had already exhibited contained pages 1-255, while this one that I was referring to contains pages from 256 to 367.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. And Mrs. Chuqing of course has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All of them put together.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: All of them on one CD. But what I wanted to say, it's two CDs which are in the exhibit list under number 16 and these are all exhumation reports from Jakarina Kosa, Pasinac, Redak, and Kevljani, and what I exhibited was photo documentation from Redak and Jakarina Kosa. These are the real exhumation reports and autopsy reports and x-ray reports, et cetera. At this moment, the CD is slightly disordered, and I want to avoid the situation with two CDs for book of missing person. So I would provide you and the Defence with better copy, and very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I have one more thing, which is -- which relates to the witness on Monday, witness 7.57. I would respectfully ask if it would be possible that we will sit on Monday longer hours, because this witness has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have discussed this already. I appreciate what Ms. Baruch pointed out last -- whenever it was, and it was already agreed to, as far as -- from our side, as far as we are concerned. I do not intend to put Mr. Ackerman at any overstressing or over pressure, too much pressure during his first week here. You have to make adjustments accordingly. Perhaps shorten the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. I only want to point out that this witness has problems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shorten out the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We can shorten out the examination-in-chief, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you need him -- yes, but if you need him out of The Hague on Monday evening, that's what you have to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: There are two parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I know that there are two parts. I am sure that Mr. Ackerman will not try to keep him longer. We'll try, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that's it. Ms. Baruch, do I take it that this is your last day here?

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think, in my own name and on behalf of Judge Janu and Judge Taya, who is not here and who I'm sure would second what I am saying, I should like to publicly thank you for your most valid and professional contribution over the past two weeks, without which we couldn't possibly have proceeded, even with the presence of Mr. Cunningham here. I do appreciate that for both of you, it must have been pretty difficult, because it's not easy to catch up with all the important points that one needs to know, all the information that one needs to know on a trial that has been going on for a year and a half, almost a year and a half. I appreciate that. And I do admire the way in which you managed to conduct the defence during these two weeks, and as I said, I want to publicly express my appreciation and gratitude. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BARUCH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And it was my pleasure to represent Mr. Ackerman's client and to serve this Court. God works in mysterious ways, so 23 years ago, Mr. Ackerman married a lawyer, and it served to benefit everybody, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we adjourn until Monday, I think it's in the morning. Thank you.
